title: Colony panel: every row now explains itself on hover
question: Does the note say enough, in the right words -- and is there a row whose note you would want to say something different?
context_md:
You asked for this on the first colony-panel card: *"the user should be able to mouse hover over some of the words and get an explanation of what it means and this could also be a way to access more detailed data."* Built, both halves.

Every row on the panel now has a note. It says **what the row is, in words** — and it carries **what did not fit on the row**: the raw counts behind each rate (`PER 1K STEP 3124` becomes *3,124 steps... over the last 3,810 frames: 11,904 steps taken*), the exact threshold behind the histogram's amber, what a trait is and which way its numbers run.

The note is drawn **beside the panel and level with the row**, not under the pointer. A box that follows the cursor covers the line it is explaining, so you end up reading the explanation having lost the thing it is about.

The shot is hovering `LOW 14 MID 23 HIGH 191 FULL 200`, which is the densest row on the page and the one I expected to be least readable cold.

I have **not** done the other half of your note — *"more better graphs might be interesting"* — yet. Say what you would want graphed and I will do it: the obvious candidates are food delivered over time beside the population strip, and the energy histogram as a moving band rather than a snapshot.
